blocks.text: As a **Cisco ACS replacement**, it gives you one place that controls who logs into every network device, from core routers to firewalls, and records every command they run.

Large networks are administered by many engineers and contractors. Alepo TACACS+ gives each of them their own login, decides on each command and records what was done. That is **enterprise device administration** with one policy and one audit trail.

blocks.text: Cisco Secure ACS has reached end of life. Alepo TACACS+ is a supported **Cisco ACS replacement**, and it also replaces local device passwords.
Our engineers move your policies and device groups, test them against your own devices and support the cutover, and GTAC engineers stay on call 24x7 afterward.

Auditors get the evidence without a project. A tamper-evident trail records every login and command and is forwarded to Splunk, Sentinel or QRadar. A control map to NIST SP 800-53 is included for auditors.

sections.h2: Contractor access removed in one step

blocks.text: When a contract ends, your team removes that person in one place. No device has to be touched.

AI Agent Assist (beta) in the TACACS+ console answers questions about who was allowed to do what, straight from the audit trail. Its recommendations are drafts only. Engineers get the answer without reading raw logs or waiting for the one person who knows the policy.

items.q: Is Cisco Secure ACS end of life?
items.a: Yes. Cisco has ended support for Secure ACS. Read: Cisco ACS end of life and what to replace it with →

items.q: What makes a good Cisco ACS replacement?
items.a: A **Cisco ACS replacement** should keep TACACS+ device administration, per-command authorization and a full audit trail, and add modern integrations such as SIEM forwarding and a REST API.
It depends on the size of your policy set and device estate. Alepo engineers plan the cutover with your team and test against your own devices first.
